The best chain is QB11-QB12-QB7, with QB12 in the middle. I read garnet's current default calibration (set f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade). It lists 28 CZ pairs. I checked every chain of two pairs that share one qubit. The QB12-QB11 pair has an IRB CZ fidelity of 0.99869. The QB12-QB7 pair has 0.99802. Their product is 0.99671, which is the highest of all the chains. The second-best chain is QB12-QB11-QB16, with a product of 0.99469.

I built a 3-qubit GHZ circuit from IQM's native gates. A GHZ state is a state where all 3 qubits are either all 0 or all 1 together. The circuit first puts QB12 into an equal mix of 0 and 1. Two CZ gates, one on QB12-QB11 and one on QB12-QB7, then copy that mix onto the other two qubits. Single-qubit rotations sit around each CZ. Then the circuit measures all 3 qubits. I simulated the circuit on my own computer first. It gives 000 half the time and 111 half the time, which is the ideal GHZ result.

I ran it on garnet:mock with 200 shots. The job ID is 01a16040-d44a-75e3-b837-54ba483b6bc8. The counts were 000: 51, 011: 46, 100: 45, and 111: 58. The mock cost 0 credits. These counts do not show a GHZ state, because the mock returns random results that do not depend on the circuit. A real garnet run should give mostly 000 and 111.

The principle is that a circuit is only as good as the physical qubits it runs on. Every two-qubit gate adds a small error. Picking the chain whose CZ fidelities have the highest product gives the GHZ state its best chance of staying entangled on real hardware.
